review_notes: I read the whole file. The only new concept is `classMultMatrix`, an integer matrix with entries given by the structure constants, indexed in the transposed order. The file itself proves that it is the image of the class sum under Mathlib's `Algebra.leftMulMatrix`, and it uses that identification (`classMultMatrix_map_intCast`, `classMultMatrix_eq_leftMulMatrix`) to derive commutativity, injectivity and `mulVec` behaviour from Mathlib's API. So it does not build a rival to `Algebra.leftMulMatrix`. It is a named ℤ-valued specialisation that works for any `[Fintype G] [DecidableEq G]` group and is meant as direct input to the character-table algorithm. It has no separate API that repeats Mathlib's. The rubric does not treat a named specialisation as a defect just because it can be expressed with existing operations. I found no practical cost, such as duplicated API or repeated conversions, that would justify consolidating it. I did not inspect `structureConstant` or `classSumBasis` in the imported file, so I cannot rule out overlap there. That would be outside this file's declarations anyway.
